gloss: to bring someone along (into); to take someone (into a place)

definitions.gloss: to bring someone along into; to take someone into a place
definitions.explanation: To lead or take a person (or animal) into a specific place. Often implies the action is somewhat secretive, inappropriate, or against rules.

examples.english: I brought the dog into the store.

examples.japanese: ⟦{部外者|ぶがいしゃ}→部外者：15595_bugaisha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{社内|しゃない}→社内：13731_shanai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{連|つ}れ{込|こ}まないで⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please don't bring outsiders into the office.
My parents told me it's dangerous to bring strangers into the house.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{連|つ}れる→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧ (to take along) and ⟦{込|こ}む→込む：00719_komu⟧ (into). The ⟦{込|こ}む→込む：00719_komu⟧ component adds a sense of going inward, into an enclosed space. Often carries a negative or cautionary nuance — bringing someone where they perhaps shouldn't be, or doing so secretly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{連|つ}れ{込|こ}む: to bring someone home
- ⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{連|つ}れ{込|こ}む: to take someone into a room
- ⟦ペット→ペット：02959_petto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{連|つ}れ{込|こ}む: to bring a pet in
- {連|つ}れ{込|こ}み⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧: no bringing others in

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{連|つ}れて→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to take someone along — neutral, no negative nuance
- ⟦{引|ひ}き{込|こ}む→引き込む：05736_hikikomu⟧: to pull in; to draw into — can be used for dragging someone into a situation
- ⟦{招|まね}き{入|い}れる→招き入れる：22620_manekiireru⟧: to invite in — positive, welcoming nuance
